                        MOTION TO CLARIFY SUA SPONTE ORDER

         The Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) of the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (the

“Commission”) respectfully moves for an order clarifying several discrete items in the Hearing

Examiner’s July 16, 2026, Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending

Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”). 1 Staff

would show the Hearing Examiners the following:

         1.      The Sua Sponte Order directed El Paso Electric Company (“EPE”) to file “a single

amended and restated Application and complete supporting filing package” within 21 days, a

deadline that will fall on August 6, 2026.2

         2.      Following EPE’s filing of its amended application, Staff is directed by the Sua

Sponte Order to review the filing and supporting materials and subsequently file a completeness

report. The purpose of Staff’s filing is to “state whether the Amended Application and supporting

materials are sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent, and technically usable.”3 This

 filing is due within seven days of EPE’s filing of its amended application and supporting

materials.4

        3.      The Sua Sponte Order contains a number of provisions applicable to Staff’s review

of EPE’s amended application filing. One such provision is decretal paragraph H, which reads as

follows:

        Staff’s review shall be limited to procedural completeness, coherence, internal
        consistency, and usability. Staff shall provide any advice or commentary on
        whether EPE’s substantive requests are reasonable, lawful, or supported by the
        weight of the evidence.5

        4.      A clarification of this provision is needed to ensure that Staff correctly interprets

these two sentences and, as a result, provides the information desired by the Hearing Examiners.

Read literally, the two sentences could contradict one another. Instead, it appears to Staff that the

second sentence was subject to a minor typographical error and that the word “not” was

unintentionally omitted. If this is correct, the second sentence would read: “Staff shall not provide

any advice or commentary on whether EPE’s substantive requests are reasonable, lawful, or

supported by the weight of the evidence.”

        5.      Additionally, decretal paragraph G(9) directs Staff to consider, as part of its review,

whether “EPE has adequately supplemented affected discovery responses.”6 Here too, Staff would

respectfully request clarification, as EPE has responded (over the course of this proceeding) to

voluminous discovery requests submitted by an array of parties. 7 Staff’s seven day deadline almost

 certainly will not afford sufficient time to review EPE’s responses to all of these discovery requests

in order to determine what should be corrected.

       6.      Prior to filing, Staff requested positions of the other parties to this docket. Positions

were as follows: CCAE, the City of Las Cruces, Dwight Eggers, and Philip B. Simpson support

the motion, and EPE concurs with the motion. Dona Ana County, NMSU, and DoD/FEA do not

oppose the motion. NMDOJ and Walmart take no position.

       Wherefore, Staff respectfully moves the Hearing Examiners for an order providing the

following clarification of the Sua Sponte Order:

   •   Confirmation that decretal paragraph H should have the word “not” in its second sentence

       or, alternatively, clarification as to the meaning of the paragraph as a whole; and

   •   Clarification as to Staff’s responsibilities with respect to reviewing EPE’s discovery

       responses, pursuant to decretal paragraph G(9).

       Dated this 3rd day of August, 2026.
